summary: Modal.Surface and Drawer.Panel declare `initialFocus` and `finalFocus`, the same props #28 gave Sheet.Panel, with the same semantics. Both forwarded `rest` to Base UI's Dialog.Popup untyped, so the props already reached the behaviour layer by accident. They were undeclared, and a rename upstream would have broken them silently. Each takes a ref or a function returning the element. A function returning null, or a ref still empty, keeps the default instead of dropping focus. Base UI's boolean and interaction-type forms are not offered, because `false` would leave focus behind the scrim. The types are restated locally as `ModalFocusTarget` and `DrawerFocusTarget` rather than shared from a lib item, because the components ship as independent source and every other behaviour-layer shape in these files (DismissDetails, the forBaseUI shim) is restated per file. check:boundaries stays green. For a Drawer the default matters more than it looks: the first tabbable element is the drag handle, which is also a close button. The browser tests put two buttons ahead of the target and assert focus lands on it and returns to a named element on Escape, in both forms, against a control case proving the defaults. Removing the mapping fails all eight.

migration.manual: A caller passing `initialFocus`/`finalFocus` through the untyped spread keeps working with a ref or a function returning an element. A boolean, or a function taking Base UI's interaction type, no longer type-checks; pass a ref or `() => element` instead.
